text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; to narrow this down, how long do these episodes typically last, and do you lose consciousness or fall during them?

text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status with Secondary Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures (Epilepsy)

The duration of 3–4 minutes, combined with post-ictal lethargy, confusion, and a pre-ictal "muddy taste" (often a metallic or salty sensation), strongly suggests this is not a typical absence seizure but rather prolonged focal impaired awareness seizures evolving into generalized tonic-clonic activity, possibly due to frontal lobe involvement or evolving generalized epilepsy.
